content.title: Switch alert expansion and keep only one alert open

check.operand: previously expanded alert collapsed while the newly opened alert is expanded

content.test_md_blob:
# Switch alert expansion and keep only one alert open

> Prove that when the user opens a second alert, the previously expanded alert collapses so no more than one alert is expanded at any time.

## Step 1

Open {{start_url}} in a browser and land on the portfolio dashboard page that contains the Alerts panel.

## Step 2

In the Alerts panel, open the alert titled "Technology concentration above target" and verify its detail is expanded inline within the list.

## Step 3

In the Alerts panel, store "Technology concentration above target" as baseline_expanded_alert while it is the currently expanded alert.

## Step 4

In the Alerts panel, open the different alert titled "NVDA crossed 52-week high".

## Step 5

Assert the alert titled "Technology concentration above target" is collapsed, the alert titled "NVDA crossed 52-week high" is expanded inline, no more than one alert is expanded in the Alerts panel, and no modal dialog is presented for the alert list.

## Step 6 — assert @verifies ac-101, ac-100, ac-102, ac-113

Confirm state-transition check: previously expanded alert collapsed while the newly opened alert is expanded (equals) — the stated promise: Opening a different alert collapses the previously expanded alert.
content.objectives_blob:
objectives:
  - objective: Open {{start_url}} in a browser and land on the portfolio dashboard page that contains the Alerts panel.
    step: 1
  - objective: In the Alerts panel, open the alert titled "Technology concentration above target" and verify its detail is expanded inline within the list.
    step: 2
  - baseline: true
    objective: In the Alerts panel, store "Technology concentration above target" as baseline_expanded_alert while it is the currently expanded alert.
    step: 3
  - objective: In the Alerts panel, open the different alert titled "NVDA crossed 52-week high".
    step: 4
  - objective: Assert the alert titled "Technology concentration above target" is collapsed, the alert titled "NVDA crossed 52-week high" is expanded inline, no more than one alert is expanded in the Alerts panel, and no modal dialog is presented for the alert list.
    step: 5
  - check:
      baseline: a different alert expanded
      expected_mode: authored
      kind: state-transition
      operand: previously expanded alert collapsed while the newly opened alert is expanded
      operator: equals
      review_required: false
      verified_against: ac-101
    objective: 'Confirm state-transition check: previously expanded alert collapsed while the newly opened alert is expanded (equals) — the stated promise: Opening a different alert collapses the previously expanded alert.'
    step: 6
scenario: Switch alert expansion and keep only one alert open
title: Switch alert expansion and keep only one alert open

# Review the default portfolio alerts feed

> Prove that the alerts panel presents the expected alert titles and the required per-alert fields with allowed severity labels.

## Step 1

Open {{start_url}} in a browser and land on the portfolio dashboard page that contains the Alerts panel.

## Step 2

On the portfolio dashboard page, inspect the visible alert rows in the Alerts panel.

## Step 3

Assert the Alerts panel includes alerts titled "Technology concentration above target", "NVDA crossed 52-week high", "Portfolio volatility increased 7.2%", "Fed rate decision tomorrow", and "Cash position below tactical minimum".

## Step 4

Assert each displayed alert row shows a severity label, a title, and a timestamp, and that every visible severity label is one of critical, warning, or info.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Scored highest because it proves the core interaction risk: opening a second alert must collapse the previously expanded alert while keeping the list non-modal and within the one-expanded-alert limit.
[value_score] Scored second because it proves the foundational inline expansion behavior and non-modal presentation for a single alert open, which every deeper interaction depends on.
[value_score] Scored third because it proves the default feed content, required per-alert fields, and named alerts the investment professional scans before interacting.

[self_critique] The written state-transition check proves the switch-path promise because the test establishes one alert as the baseline expanded state before opening a different alert and then observes the first collapse and the second remain expanded. State / flow is the right technique for this sequential interaction, no stronger negative case was available in the source, and the final assertion stayed limited to the observable list state rather than inventing detail content.

[self_critique] The written state-transition check proves the base expansion promise because the test records the collapsed baseline before opening the alert and then verifies the inline expanded outcome. State / flow fits this single-step interaction, no negative invalid-input path exists in the source, and the assertion stays narrow to inline expansion, one-open limit, and non-modal presentation.

[self_critique] The written presence check proves the feed-content promise because it verifies the exact named alert set from the committed AC, while the steps separately cover required fields and allowed severity labels. Equivalence partitioning fits the fixed content review, a negative list-content path is absent because the PRD states no alternate or exclusion behavior, and the assertions avoid unstated promises such as sorting, counts beyond the named set, or dismissibility rules.
